title: Blue screen 0x139 KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE while gaming
summary: Windows detected corrupted data inside the kernel. The usual suspects are unstable RAM settings or a bad driver, especially after a hardware change.
cause: This bugcheck fires when an internal Windows data structure is damaged. Memory overclocks (XMP/EXPO), mixed RAM kits, and faulty drivers are the most common causes. It often appears right after new hardware is installed.
steps: If you just changed hardware, undo the most recent change first and see if the blue screens stop.
Disable XMP/EXPO in the BIOS (or lower the memory speed one step) and test for a day.
Run a memory test such as TestMem5 or MemTest86. Any error means a RAM or memory-setting problem.
Update chipset and GPU drivers from the manufacturers' sites.
Open an admin Command Prompt and run 'sfc /scannow', then 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth'.
ifStillBroken: Open the minidump (C:\Windows\Minidump) with WinDbg or BlueScreenView to see which driver is named, or send it to OldWolfDev for a personal review.

affiliate.text: Matched RAM kits run more stable than mixed sticks
